principles: Existing-project init should be minimally invasive by default.
Starter/demo code should be explicit and reversible, not an accidental side effect.
Configuration detection must observe the project before Koala writes optional files.
Smoke tests should encode user-visible init contracts, not only internal asset presence.
drivers: User confusion comes from init creating unused src files in projects that already have their own structure.
Python projects without src are misdetected because init creates src before scanRoot detection.
The previous starter templates are still useful for fresh demos and should remain available behind a clear flag.

options.name: A: Default management-only init with --starter aliases for legacy templates
pros: Stops default project pollution while keeping Koala management assets installed.
Preserves old starter behavior for users who explicitly ask for it.
Lets scanRoot detection use the pre-init project shape.
cons: Changes default output, so help text and entrypoint smoke must make the new contract obvious.
Users who expected starter files by default now need to pass a flag.

options.name: B: Keep default starter files and only patch Python scanRoot
pros: Smallest code change and minimal disruption for old demo users.
Would fix the immediate Python scanRoot misconfiguration.
cons: Still creates unused business src files, which is the user-facing problem.
Leaves README/help implying init owns application source layout.

options.name: C: Add separate flags for source templates and test templates
pros: More granular control over src templates versus tests directory.
Could preserve tests by default while moving only src files.
cons: More CLI surface than the problem needs.
Keeps ambiguity about which files are Koala management assets versus starter/demo assets.

chosen: A: Default management-only init with --starter aliases for legacy templates
rationale: Choose the management-only default because it directly matches the user complaint: koala init should install Koala workflow assets without inventing an application src layout. Treating --starter and --with-template as aliases keeps the old scaffold available without polluting existing projects.

preMortem.scenario: Help text still says src/core and src/shells are default init outputs.
preMortem.trigger: A user runs koala init --help after the change.
preMortem.consequence: The CLI behavior is fixed but UX remains misleading, repeating the status-message class of bug.
preMortem.mitigation: Update help text and assert the starter flag is documented in entrypoint smoke.

preMortem.scenario: scanRoot is still computed after optional directories are created.
preMortem.trigger: A Python project without src runs init with the new default path.
preMortem.consequence: koala.config.json still records scanRoot=src even though src is not a real project source root.
preMortem.mitigation: Capture hadSrcBeforeInit before creating optional starter dirs and add a Python smoke assertion for scanRoot=.

preMortem.scenario: Default init no longer creates src but still creates tests, which users view as the same pollution class.
preMortem.trigger: Existing projects run default koala init and see a new tests directory.
preMortem.consequence: The visible complaint is only partially fixed.
preMortem.mitigation: Treat tests as starter/demo asset too; keep testsDir in config but do not create the directory by default.

preMortem.scenario: Only one flag spelling works in one entrypoint path.
preMortem.trigger: Users run npx koala-init --with-template or node packages/main/dist/cli.js init --starter.
preMortem.consequence: The opt-in contract is inconsistent and support burden grows.
preMortem.mitigation: Parse both --starter and --with-template from shared initArgs and cover at least the core CLI spelling in smoke.
